scope: Sources consulted for the six discriminating tests, with what was actually read. A listed source is not a completed methodological audit unless stated.

sources.citation: Du, A. et al. (2023). Ground magnetic survey on Mars from the Zhurong rover. Nature Astronomy 7, 1037.
sources.consulted: Publisher abstract and main-text figures/values: 16 sites along a 1,089 m track at 25.066° N, 109.926° E; horizontal 3.4–24.0 nT, total 5.2–39.8 nT, mean horizontal 11.2 ± 10.9 nT; L19 model continued to the ground 81 nT total and 55 nT horizontal.
sources.note: Our own continuation gives 79 and 53 nT, agreeing with the published values.

sources.citation: Mittelholz, A. & Johnson, C. L. (2022). The Martian crustal magnetic field. Frontiers in Astronomy and Space Sciences 9, 895362.
sources.consulted: Open-access full text, sections 2, 4.1 and 4.2: InSight surface field about 2,000 nT; MGS-only model about 200 nT and L19 about 600 nT at the site per their Figure 3; Parker (2003) minimum 4.76 A/m over 50 km; dynamo active 4.5 to at least 3.7 Ga in recent interpretations; Gong & Wieczorek depths 9 km north, 32 km south, >40 km under Sirenum/Cimmeria.
sources.note: Our L19 evaluation at InSight gives about 310 nT at degree 134; the review quotes about 600 nT for a model including MAVEN data. The difference is recorded, not resolved.

sources.citation: Steele, S. C. et al. (2024). Reversing Martian dynamo and basin magnetization. Nature Communications 15.
sources.consulted: Open-access full text: 420 random reversal histories with mean frequencies 0–10 per Myr; basins 200–2,200 km; cooling 10–500 Myr; saturation remanences 0.02–0.5 A m² kg⁻¹; Curie depth about 50 km for magnetite; conclusion that rates ≥ 1.5 per Myr leave >90% of basins >800 km apparently demagnetized; dynamo active until at least 3.9–3.7 Ga.
sources.note: We use their reversal-rate threshold as an external comparison, not as an input.

sources.citation: Gong, S. & Wieczorek, M. (2021). Depth of Martian magnetization from localized power spectrum analysis. JGR Planets 126.
sources.consulted: Publisher abstract, Zenodo README and the three data files (best fit, 1-sigma lower and upper): equivalent depths of thin layers, 20° windows, bandwidth 17, 150 km altitude, best-fit cap radius, depth, magnetization metric and reduced chi-squared.
sources.note: The full-text description of the magnetized-caps model could not be retrieved in this pass; the layer geometries used in Test 3 are our own declared alternatives around the equivalent depth.

sources.citation: Wieczorek, M. A. et al. (2022). InSight constraints on the global character of the Martian crust. JGR Planets 127.
sources.consulted: Archive README, dichotomy and constant-density summary spreadsheets (Khan2022 rows), boundary polyline and the 39 km / 2,900–2,900 thickness grid used as validation target.
sources.note: Our inversion reproduces their equal-density grid within about 4.4 km RMS; their hydrostatic treatment and depth-dependent mantle density were not audited.

sources.citation: Thiriet, M., Michaut, C., Breuer, D. & Plesa, A.-C. (2018). Hemispheric dichotomy in lithosphere thickness on Mars caused by differences in crustal structure and composition. JGR Planets 123, 823–848.
sources.consulted: figshare products: present-day North/South temperature profiles (BestModel, Min, Max), elastic-thickness evolution files and the compiled elastic-thickness constraints; publisher abstract values (Noachian Te ≈ 25 km south; ≥300 km north and >110 km south today under the polar caps; 55–65% of radioelements in the crust).
sources.note: The paper's model parameters were not retrieved; our thermal parameters are declared ranges constrained by their published present-day profiles.

sources.citation: Goossens, S. & Sabaka, T. (2026). Mars crustal density and thickness from gravity with a boundary constraint. NASA PGDA product 102.
sources.consulted: Producer summary: north 2,622 ± 42 kg/m³, south 2,492 ± 36 kg/m³.
sources.note: Their covariance and journal methods were not audited; the densities enter as a declared scenario.

sources.citation: Kim, D. et al. (2023). Global crustal thickness revealed by surface waves orbiting Mars. GRL 50.
sources.consulted: Abstract (earlier project pass): most tested models with crustal density contrasts above 200 kg/m³ excluded; mean thickness 42–56 km.
sources.note: The ±200 kg/m³ scenarios bracket their bound.

sources.citation: Tanaka, K. L. et al. (2014). Geologic map of Mars. USGS SIM 3292.
sources.consulted: Unit codes and descriptions from the USGS feature service already in the project snapshot.
sources.note: Epoch classes are ordinal; declared class-centre ages are reading aids only.

sources.citation: Langlais, B. et al. (2019). A new model of the crustal magnetic field of Mars using MGS and MAVEN. JGR Planets 124.
sources.consulted: Coefficient file (Zenodo 3876714) and normalization conventions checked with an axial-dipole test in the earlier project pass.

sources.citation: Genova, A. et al. (2016). Seasonal and static gravity field of Mars from MGS, Mars Odyssey and MRO radio science. Icarus 272.
sources.consulted: GMM-3 coefficient file from NASA PDS via pyshtools.

sources.citation: Wieczorek, M. A. & Phillips, R. J. (1998). Potential anomalies on a sphere: applications to the thickness of the lunar crust. JGR 103, 1715–1724.
sources.consulted: Equations 10 and 18 as documented in the pyshtools reference; our implementation was validated against the library's constant-density routine.
